segments.arabic: [779] حدثنا معلى بن أسد قال: حدثنا وهيب عن عبد الله بن طاوس عن أبيه عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Mu‘alla ibn Asad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة أعظم على الجبهة وأشار بيده على أنفه واليدين والركبتين وأطراف القدمين ولا نكفت الثياب والشعر
segments.english: I was commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead (and he pointed with his hand to his nose), the two hands, the two knees and the tips of the feet; and we do not gather up clothing or hair.

notes: The gesture is retained in parentheses as a narrator description, not quoted as a spoken command. The singular command and plural we do not gather follow the selected Arabic; the English comparisons use my clothing instead. No tip of the nose is added to this report.

segments.arabic: [780] حدثنا موسى قال: حدثنا همام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة قال
segments.english: Musa related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said:

segments.arabic: انطلقت إلى أبي سعيد الخدري فقلت: ألا تخرج بنا إلى النخل نتحدث فخرج، فقال: قلت: حدثني ما سمعت من النبي ﷺ في ليلة القدر قال اعتكف رسول الله ﷺ عشر الأول من رمضان واعتكفنا معه فأتاه جبريل، فقال إن الذي تطلب أمامك فاعتكف العشر الأوسط فاعتكفنا معه فأتاه جبريل، فقال إن الذي تطلب أمامك قام النبي ﷺ خطيبا صبيحة عشرين من رمضان، فقال من كان اعتكف مع النبي ﷺ فليرجع فإني أريت ليلة القدر وإني نسيتها وإنها في العشر الأواخر في وتر وإني رأيت كأني أسجد في طين وماء وكان سقف المسجد جريد النخل وما نرى في السماء شيئا فجاءت قزعة فأمطرنا فصلى بنا النبي ﷺ حتى رأيت أثر الطين والماء على جبهة رسول الله ﷺ وأرنبته تصديق رؤياه
segments.english: I went to Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri and said, “Will you not come out with us to the palm trees so we can talk?” He went out. He said: I said, “Relate to me what you heard from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about the Night of Decree.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, observed retreat during the first ten of Ramadan, and we observed retreat with him. Jibril came to him and said, “What you seek lies ahead of you.” Then he observed retreat during the middle ten, and we observed retreat with him. Jibril came to him and said, “What you seek lies ahead of you.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to address the people on the morning of the twentieth of Ramadan. He said, “Whoever observed retreat with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, should return. I was shown the Night of Decree, and I forgot it. It is among the last ten, on an odd night. I saw as though I were prostrating in mud and water.” The mosque’s roof was palm branches, and we saw nothing in the sky. Then a cloud came, and rain fell on us. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in prayer until I saw the trace of mud and water on the forehead of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the tip of his nose, confirming his dream.

notes: Both visits of Jibril, both shared retreats and all six honorifics remain. Return follows فليرجع, rather than replacing it with continue. The selected I saw and mud-and-water order remain; the historical print reverses the last pair. No explicit date is inserted after forgot it.

segments.arabic: [781] حدثنا محمد بن كثير قال: أخبرنا سفيان عن أبي حازم عن سهل بن سعد قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d, who said:

segments.arabic: كان الناس يصلون مع النبي ﷺ وهم عاقدوا أزرهم من الصغر على رقابهم فقيل للنساء لا ترفعن رؤوسكن حتى يستوي الرجال جلوسا
segments.english: People used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with their waist wrappers tied around their necks because they were small. The women were told, “Do not raise your heads until the men are sitting upright.”

notes: The passive women were told is preserved without assigning the instruction to a named speaker.

segments.arabic: [782] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد وهو ابن زيد عن عمرو بن دينار عن طاوس عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad—who is Ibn Zayd—related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: أمر النبي ﷺ أن يسجد على سبعة أعظم ولا يكف ثوبه ولا شعره
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to prostrate on seven bones and not to gather up his clothing or his hair.

notes: Both vocalised prints support was commanded. The commander is not named in the selected wording. The identification who is Ibn Zayd remains in its chain position.

segments.arabic: أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة لا أكف شعرا ولا ثوبا

segments.arabic: [784] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن سفيان قال: حدثني منصور عن مسلم عن مسروق عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها أنها قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, who said: Mansur related to me, from Muslim, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يكثر أن يقول: في ركوعه وسجوده سبحانك اللهم ربنا وبحمدك اللهم اغفر لي
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, frequently said in his bowing and prostration, “Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me.”

segments.arabic: يتأول القرآن
segments.english: He was putting the Quran into practice.

notes: The closing clause is a narrator description, not part of the supplication. Al-Ayni explains it as carrying out what the Quran commands. The historical print expands Mansur and Muslim; the selected short names remain.

segments.arabic: [785] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة أن مالك بن الحويرث قال لأصحابه
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith said to his companions:

segments.arabic: ألا أنبئكم صلاة رسول الله ﷺ قال: وذاك في غير حين صلاة فقام ثم ركع فكبر ثم رفع رأسه فقام هنية ثم سجد ثم رفع رأسه هنية فصلى صلاة عمرو بن سلمة شيخنا هذا
segments.english: “Shall I tell you about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said: That was not at a time for prayer. He stood, then bowed and said the takbir. Then he raised his head and stood briefly, then prostrated, then raised his head briefly. He prayed the prayer of ‘Amr ibn Salimah, this shaykh of ours.

segments.arabic: قال أيوب كان يفعل شيئا لم أرهم يفعلونه كان يقعد في الثالثة والرابعة
segments.english: Ayyub said: He used to do something that I did not see them doing: he used to sit in the third and fourth rak‘ahs.

segments.arabic: قال: فأتينا النبي ﷺ فأقمنا عنده، فقال لو رجعتم إلى أهليكم صلوا صلاة كذا في حين كذا صلوا صلاة كذا في حين كذا فإذا حضرت الصلاة فليؤذن أحدكم وليؤمكم أكبركم
segments.english: He said: We came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and stayed with him. He said, “If you would return to your families: pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time; pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time. When prayer is due, let one of you give the call to prayer, and let the eldest of you lead you.”

notes: Both printed witnesses read third OR fourth; the selected digital text and Bewley read AND. Ibn al-Mulaqqin explicitly records both variants and attributes the and reading to a transmitted version, while also reporting criticism of it. This is retained as a documented variant, not silently corrected as a copying error. Ibn Hajar discusses or as narrator uncertainty and identifies the resumed We came as Malik’s speech. No explanatory replacement such as between the third and fourth is inserted.

The modern print gives the two parts separate report labels 818 and 819; the complete selected digital report and both English comparisons keep them together. The repeated such-and-such instruction remains twice. Salimah follows the inspected vocalisation سَلِمَة; the chain retains Hammad without adding Ibn Zayd.

segments.arabic: [786] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحيم قال: حدثنا أبو أحمد محمد بن عبد الله الزبيري قال: حدثنا مسعر عن الحكم عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى عن البراء قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Zubayri related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us, from al-Hakam, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara’, who said:

segments.arabic: كان سجود النبي ﷺ وركوعه وقعوده بين السجدتين قريبا من السواء
segments.english: The prostration of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his bowing and his sitting between the two prostrations were approximately equal in length.

notes: All three actions remain, without adding exceptions from other reports. The full Abu Ahmad identification is retained.

segments.arabic: [787] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن ثابت عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: إني لا آلو أن أصلي بكم كما رأيت النبي ﷺ يصلي بنا
segments.english: I spare no effort to lead you in prayer as I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lead us in prayer.

segments.arabic: قال ثابت كان أنس يصنع شيئا لم أركم تصنعونه كان إذا رفع رأسه من الركوع قام حتى يقول القائل قد نسي وبين السجدتين حتى يقول القائل قد نسي
segments.english: Thabit said: Anas used to do something I have not seen you doing. When he raised his head from bowing, he would stand until someone would say, “He has forgotten”; and between the two prostrations, until someone would say, “He has forgotten.”

notes: Both repeated forgotten clauses remain without supplying a forgotten action from a comparison edition. The historical print expands Anas to Anas ibn Malik; the selected short name is unchanged.

segments.arabic: [788] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا محمد بن جعفر قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: سمعت قتادة عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: اعتدلوا في السجود ولا يبسط أحدكم ذراعيه انبساط الكلب
segments.english: Be balanced in prostration, and none of you should spread his forearms as a dog spreads them.

notes: Related to us for Shubah follows the selected text and modern print; the historical print has informed us. The separate Abu Humayd chapter introduction is not appended to this numbered report.

segments.arabic: [789] حدثنا محمد بن الصباح قال: أخبرنا هشيم قال: أخبرنا خالد الحذاء عن أبي قلابة قال: أخبرنا مالك بن الحويرث الليثي
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us. He said: Hushaym informed us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ informed us, from Abu Qilabah, who said: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith al-Laythi informed us:

segments.arabic: أنه رأى النبي ﷺ يصلي فإذا كان في وتر من صلاته لم ينهض حتى يستوي قاعدا
segments.english: He saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying. When he was in an odd-numbered rak‘ah of his prayer, he did not rise until he was sitting upright.

notes: The phrase في وتر من صلاته means an odd-numbered part of the prayer here. The Khan-family comparison says odd rakahs; Bewley instead calls this the Witr prayer. That restriction is not imported into the working translation or chapter title.

segments.arabic: [790] حدثنا معلى بن أسد قال: حدثنا وهيب عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة قال
segments.english: Mu‘alla ibn Asad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

segments.arabic: جاءنا مالك بن الحويرث فصلى بنا في مسجدنا هذا، فقال إني لأصلي بكم وما أريد الصلاة ولكن أريد أن أريكم كيف رأيت النبي ﷺ يصلي
segments.english: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith came to us and led us in prayer in this mosque of ours. He said, “I am leading you in prayer, but I do not intend the prayer; I want to show you how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray.”

segments.arabic: قال أيوب فقلت لأبي قلابة وكيف كانت صلاته قال مثل صلاة شيخنا هذا يعني عمرو بن سلمة قال أيوب وكان ذلك الشيخ يتم التكبير وإذا رفع رأسه عن السجدة الثانية جلس واعتمد على الأرض ثم قام
segments.english: Ayyub said: I asked Abu Qilabah, “What was his prayer like?” He said, “Like the prayer of this shaykh of ours,” meaning ‘Amr ibn Salimah. Ayyub said: That shaykh used to complete the takbir. When he raised his head from the second prostration, he sat, supported himself on the ground, then stood.

notes: The first assertion I am leading you is retained, as is the contrast with his stated intention. Both Ayyub attributions and the second-prostration sequence remain. Salimah follows the inspected vocalisation.

segments.arabic: [791] حدثنا يحيى بن صالح قال: حدثنا فليح بن سليمان عن سعيد بن الحارث قال
segments.english: Yahya ibn Salih related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى لنا أبو سعيد فجهر بالتكبير حين رفع رأسه من السجود وحين سجد وحين رفع وحين قام من الركعتين، وقال هكذا رأيت النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Abu Sa‘id led us in prayer. He said the takbir aloud when he raised his head from prostration, when he prostrated, when he rose and when he stood after the two rak‘ahs. He said, “This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: All four occasions and aloud remain. The selected text and modern print end without يفعل; the historical print includes it. No doing is added from the latter.

segments.arabic: [792] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد قال: حدثنا غيلان بن جرير عن مطرف قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: Ghaylan ibn Jarir related to us, from Mutarrif, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت أنا وعمران صلاة خلف علي بن أبي طالب رضى الله تعالى عنه فكان إذا سجد كبر وإذا رفع كبر وإذا نهض من الركعتين كبر فلما سلم أخذ عمران بيدي، فقال لقد صلى بنا هذا صلاة محمد ﷺ أو قال لقد ذكرني هذا صلاة محمد ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Imran and I prayed a prayer behind ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When he prostrated, he said the takbir; when he rose, he said the takbir; and when he stood after the two rak‘ahs, he said the takbir. When he said the closing greeting, ‘Imran took my hand and said, “This man has led us in the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace”; or he said, “This has reminded me of the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: The alternatives stay in the selected order, with us in the first and me in the second. Bewley reverses their order and expands Imran to Ibn Husayn; neither change is imported. Both prophetic honorifics remain.

segments.arabic: [793] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن عبد الله أنه أخبره
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from ‘Abdullah, who informed him:

segments.arabic: أنه كان يرى عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما يتربع في الصلاة إذا جلس ففعلته وأنا يومئذ حديث السن فنهاني عبد الله بن عمر، وقال إنما سنة الصلاة أن تنصب رجلك اليمنى وتثني اليسرى فقلت: إنك تفعل ذلك، فقال إن رجلي لا تحملاني
segments.english: He used to see ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, sitting cross-legged when he sat in prayer. I did so, being young at the time. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar forbade me and said, “The practice of prayer is to set your right foot upright and bend the left.” I said, “But you do that.” He said, “My legs do not support me.”

notes: Both printed witnesses expand the last chain name to Abdullah ibn Abdullah. The selected shorter Abdullah remains, with the expansion recorded separately rather than silently inserted. The change from he used to see to I did so is retained.

segments.arabic: [794] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن خالد عن سعيد عن محمد بن عمرو بن حلحلة عن محمد بن عمرو بن عطاء
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Khalid, from Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Halhalah, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Ata’.

segments.arabic: وحدثنا الليث عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب ويزيد بن محمد عن محمد بن عمرو بن حلحلة عن محمد بن عمرو بن عطاء
segments.english: And al-Layth related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib and Yazid ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Halhalah, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Ata’:

segments.arabic: أنه كان جالسا مع نفر من أصحاب النبي ﷺ فذكرنا صلاة النبي ﷺ، فقال أبو حميد الساعدي أنا كنت أحفظكم لصلاة رسول الله ﷺ رأيته إذا كبر جعل يديه حذاء منكبيه وإذا ركع أمكن يديه من ركبتيه ثم هصر ظهره فإذا رفع رأسه استوى حتى يعود كل فقار مكانه فإذا سجد وضع يديه غير مفترش ولا قابضهما واستقبل بأطراف أصابع رجليه القبلة فإذا جلس في الركعتين جلس على رجله اليسرى ونصب اليمنى وإذا جلس في الركعة الآخرة قدم رجله اليسرى ونصب الأخرى وقعد على مقعدته
segments.english: He was sitting with a group of the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. We mentioned the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Humayd al-Sa‘idi said, “I remembered the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, better than any of you. I saw that when he said the takbir, he put his hands level with his shoulders. When he bowed, he placed his hands firmly on his knees, then bent his back. When he raised his head, he stood upright until every vertebra returned to its place. When he prostrated, he placed his hands down, neither spreading them out flat nor drawing them in close, and pointed the tips of his toes towards the qiblah. When he sat after the two rak‘ahs, he sat on his left foot and set the right upright. When he sat in the last rak‘ah, he brought his left foot forward, set the other upright and sat on his buttocks.”

segments.arabic: وسمع الليث يزيد بن أبي حبيب ويزيد من محمد بن حلحلة وابن حلحلة من ابن عطاء قال أبو صالح عن الليث كل فقار، وقال ابن المبارك عن يحيى بن أيوب قال: حدثني يزيد بن أبي حبيب أن محمد بن عمرو حدثه كل فقار
segments.english: Al-Layth heard Yazid ibn Abi Habib; Yazid heard Muhammad ibn Halhalah; and Ibn Halhalah heard Ibn ‘Ata’. Abu Salih said, from al-Layth: “Every vertebra.” Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, who said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib related to me that Muhammad ibn ‘Amr related to him: “Every vertebra.”

notes: Both complete opening chains and all closing hearing links and named routes remain. The selected unvocalised كل فقار is repeated twice at the close and is translated twice; no apparent duplication is removed. Ibn al-Mulaqqin discusses variant vocalisations and a consonant-order variant, which are not inserted into the selected Arabic.

The historical print expands Said and the final Muhammad name and adds مكانه to the Abu Salih phrase. The selected short names and phrase remain. The third-person he was sitting and first-person we mentioned remain.

segments.arabic: [795] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: حدثني عبد الرحمن بن هرمز مولى بني عبد المطلب، وقال مرة مولى ربيعة بن الحارث أن عبد الله بن بحينة وهو من أزد شنوءة وهو حليف لبني عبد مناف وكان من أصحاب النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz related to me—a client of Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib (on one occasion he said: a client of Rabi‘ah ibn al-Harith)—from ‘Abdullah ibn Buhaynah, who was from Azd Shanu’ah, was an ally of Banu ‘Abd Manaf and was one of the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ صلى بهم الظهر فقام في الركعتين الأوليين لم يجلس فقام الناس معه حتى إذا قضى الصلاة وانتظر الناس تسليمه كبر وهو جالس فسجد سجدتين قبل أن يسلم ثم سلم
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led them in the noon prayer. He stood after the first two rak‘ahs without sitting, and the people stood with him. When he had completed the prayer and the people awaited his closing greeting, he said the takbir while sitting, then made two prostrations before saying the closing greeting. Then he said the closing greeting.

notes: The two client affiliations stay in the chain in their original order, with the on-one-occasion variant intact. The two prophetic honorifics, tribal affiliation, alliance and before/then greeting sequence remain.

segments.arabic: [796] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا بكر عن جعفر بن ربيعة عن الأعرج عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة قال
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Bakr related to us, from Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah, from al-A‘raj, from ‘Abdullah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى بنا رسول الله ﷺ الظهر فقام وعليه جلوس فلما كان في آخر صلاته سجد سجدتين وهو جالس
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the noon prayer. He stood when he should have sat. At the end of his prayer, he made two prostrations while sitting.

notes: The selected short Bakr name remains. No second-rakah, tashahhud or forgetfulness explanation from another rendition is inserted.

segments.arabic: [797] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا الأعمش عن شقيق بن سلمة قال: قال عبد الله
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, who said: ‘Abdullah said:

segments.arabic: كنا إذا صلينا خلف النبي ﷺ قلنا السلام على جبريل وميكائيل السلام على فلان وفلان فالتفت إلينا رسول الله ﷺ، فقال إن الله هو السلام فإذا صلى أحدكم فليقل التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين فإنكم إذا قلتموها أصابت كل عبد لله صالح في السماء والأرض أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله
segments.english: When we prayed behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, we used to say, “Peace be upon Jibril and Mika’il. Peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, turned to us and said, “Allah is Peace. When one of you prays, let him say: ‘Greetings belong to Allah, and prayers and good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah’s righteous servants.’ When you say this, it reaches every righteous servant of Allah in heaven and earth. ‘I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.’”

notes: The selected greetings, prayers and good things order remains. The middle explanation stays inside the reported speech, between the greeting and testimony. The first Prophet title follows the selected text and modern print; the historical print has Messenger there. No extra honorific is added inside the testimony.

segments.arabic: [798] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرنا عروة بن الزبير عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ أخبرته
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed us, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يدعو في الصلاة اللهم إني أعوذ بك من عذاب القبر وأعوذ بك من فتنة المسيح الدجال وأعوذ بك من فتنة المحيا وفتنة الممات اللهم إني أعوذ بك من المأثم والمغرم، فقال له قائل ما أكثر ما تستعيذ من المغرم، فقال إن الرجل إذا غرم حدث فكذب ووعد فأخلف
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate in prayer: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the false messiah, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of life and the trial of death. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and debt.” Someone said to him, “How often you seek refuge from debt!” He said, “When a man falls into debt, he speaks and lies, and he promises and breaks his promise.”

segments.arabic: وعن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة أن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يستعيذ في صلاته من فتنة الدجال
segments.english: And from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seek refuge in his prayer from the trial of the Dajjal.

notes: All four refuge clauses and the complete final Zuhri–Urwah–Aishah route remain, including informed us in the opening and informed me at the close. The modern print numbers the closing route separately as 833; the selected source and English comparisons keep it with the preceding supplication.

The historical print additionally contains a Muhammad ibn Yusuf/Khalaf ibn Amir note about pronouncing the two Masih names, and expands the final Urwah to Ibn al-Zubayr. These are absent from the selected digital text and modern print; they are recorded as witness differences, not silently inserted.

segments.arabic: [799] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا الليث عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب عن أبي الخير عن عبد الله بن عمرو عن أبي بكر الصديق رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أنه قال لرسول الله ﷺ علمني دعاء أدعو به في صلاتي قال قل اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي ظلما كثيرا ولا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت فاغفر لي مغفرة من عندك وارحمني إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم
segments.english: He said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer.” He said, “Say: ‘O Allah, I have greatly wronged myself, and no one forgives sins but You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me. You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.’”

notes: The complete request and forgiveness-from-You clause remain. Abdullah ibn Amr is not confused with Ibn Umar.
